{{Current events|year=2026|month=02|day=20|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)|Hezbollah–Israel conflict]]
***At least 12 people are killed and 33 others are injured in multiple [[Israel]]i strikes targeting members of [[Hezbollah]] and [[Hamas]] across Lebanon. One Hezbollah leader has been reported deceased. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/20/one-killed-in-israeli-strike-on-largest-palestinian-refugee-camp-in-lebanon (Al Jazeera)] [https://imemc.org/article/12-killed-in-israeli-strikes-across-lebanon/ (IMEMC)] [https://globalnation.inquirer.net/309804/lebanon-says-8-dead-in-israeli-strikes-on-east-south (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[Crimea attacks]]
***One person is killed and several buildings are damaged in [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[drone warfare|drone strikes]] in [[Sevastopol]], [[Crimea]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/one-dead-ukrainian-attack-sevastopol-crimea-governor-says-2026-02-20 (Reuters)]
*[[Operation Southern Spear]]
**[[United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear]]
***Three people are killed in a strike by the [[United States Southern Command]] on an alleged [[Illegal drug trade|drug trafficking vessel]] in an area of the eastern [[Pacific Ocean]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/21/us-military-says-it-attacked-vessel-in-pacific-ocean-killing-three-people (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**At least 50 people are killed and women and children [[kidnapping in Nigeria|are abducted]] in overnight attacks by gunmen on a village in [[Bukkuyum|Bukkuyum LGA]], [[Zamfara State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/attackers-kill-least-50-abduct-women-children-nigerias-zamfara-state-2026-02-20 (Reuters)] [https://english.news.cn/20260221/2c252d83898c46258632a6a2c308b101/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The [[Sagrada Família]] in [[Barcelona]], [[Spain]], reaches its designed height of {{convert|172.5|m|ft|abbr=off}} after beginning construction in 1882, ahead of the completion of the main building expected later in 2026. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/feb/20/barcelona-sagrada-familias-church-central-tower-put-in-place (''The Guardian'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Seven people are killed, including a pregnant woman, two children are injured and 3,000 are displaced in three [[landslide]]s in the [[Provinces of the Philippines|provinces]] of [[Davao Oriental]] and [[Davao de Oro]], [[Philippines]]. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/climate-and-environment/article/torrential-rains-unleash-landslides-that-kill-7-in-southern-philippines (CTV News)] [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2184520/4-dead-in-mati-landslide (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')] [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2184590/2-children-rescued-in-surigao-del-sur-landslide (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*Seven [[China|Chinese]] [[tourism in Russia|tourists]] are killed after their van sinks into a frozen-over section of [[Lake Baikal]] on [[Olkhon Island]], [[Irkutsk Oblast]], [[Russia]]. One person was able to escape the vehicle and reach the surface. An investigation into criminal negligence and safety violations is opened. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/02/20/chinese-tourists-drown-in-lake-baikal-after-van-falls-through-ice-a92008 (''The Moscow Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/eight-feared-dead-after-bus-with-chinese-tourists-sinks-into-russias-lake-baikal-2026-02-20/ (Reuters)]
*Seven people are killed and two others are injured in a collision between a van and a truck in [[Valsad district]], [[Gujarat]], [[India]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/seven-killed-2-injure-after-van-collides-with-truck-on-hilly-stretch-in-gujarat-101771601377249.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
*Five people are killed, another is injured and power outages are reported during a major snowstorm in [[Linz]] and [[Tyrol (state)|Tyrol]], [[Austria]]. [https://globalnation.inquirer.net/309811/austria-snowstorm-leaves-five-dead-road-and-power-chaos (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*The [[France|French]] [[Ministry of Agriculture (France)|agriculture ministry]] authorizes the [[culling]] of around 200 wolves, raising the annual [[Nuisance wildlife management|removal limit]] to 21% of the estimated population of over 1,000 animals, with a possible increase to 23%, citing rising [[livestock]] losses as wolf numbers expand into agricultural areas and [[Regions of France|regions]] near [[List of communes in France with over 20,000 inhabitants|major cities]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/france-allows-culling-around-200-wolves-protect-livestock-2026-02-20/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Galápagos National Park]] releases 158 [[Captive breeding|captive-bred]] juvenile [[Galápagos tortoise|giant tortoises]] onto [[Floreana Island]] in the [[Galápagos Islands]] of [[Ecuador]], marking the species' return more than 180 years after its local extinction in the 1840s. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9wn1jrzk4go (BBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2026 Iran–United States crisis]]
**[[Norway]] relocates some of its approximately 60 [[Norwegian Armed Forces|military]] personnel [[Norwegian military operations abroad|stationed]] in [[Iraq]] and other parts of the [[Middle East]] back to Norway and other regional locations, citing security concerns amid heightened tensions between [[Iran]] and the [[United States]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/norway-moves-some-its-60-soldiers-middle-east-due-security-situation-2026-02-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[Chile–China relations]], [[Chile–United States relations]], [[China–United States trade war]]
**The [[United States]] revokes the [[Visa policy of the United States|visas]] of three [[Chile]]an officials, including [[Ministry of Transport and Telecommunications (Chile)|telecommunications minister]] [[Juan Carlos Muñoz (politician)|Juan Carlos Muñoz]], after Chile agreed to build a [[submarine cable]] with [[China]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-20/us-restricts-visas-for-chile-officials-citing-regional-security (Bloomberg)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 Thai protests]]
**A [[Thailand|Thai]] [[Judiciary of Thailand|court]] sentences activist lawyer [[Arnon Nampa]], who has been detained since 2023, to an additional two years and eight months in prison for violating the country's ''[[Lèse-majesté in Thailand|lèse-majesté]]'' law over remarks made at a 2020 rally. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/thai-court-extends-sentence-lawyer-who-called-monarchy-reform-2026-02-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[Tariffs in the second Trump administration]]
**The [[United States]] [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]] rules in ''[[Learning Resources v. Trump]]'' that the [[International Emergency Economic Powers Act]] does not grant the [[President of the United States|President]] the power to impose trade [[tariff]]s. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/02/20/politics/supreme-court-tariffs (CNN)]
**U.S. president [[Donald Trump]] signs [[executive order]]s aimed at implementing tariffs using Section 122 and [[Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974|Section 301]] of the [[Trade Act of 1974]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/trump-orders-temporary-10-global-tariff-replace-duties-struck-down-by-us-supreme-2026-02-20/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*The [[Florida Legislature]], in the United States, passes a measure to [[List of things named after Donald Trump|formally rename]] [[Palm Beach International Airport]] in [[Palm Beach County, Florida]], as the "President [[Donald Trump|Donald J. Trump]] International Airport". [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/feb/20/palm-beach-airport-renamed-donald-trump (''The Guardian'')]  [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-20/palm-beach-airport-to-be-renamed-donald-j-trump-international (Bloomberg)] [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/us/news/2026/02/20/florida-airport-renamed-donald-trump/ (''The Telegraph'')]

*Clashes in [[Tirana]] breakout between [[Riot Police]] and opposition party protesters demanding [[Edi Rama]]'s resignation due to allegations of [[Belinda Balluku]]'s corruption on the anniversary of [[Fall of communism in Albania|Enver Hoxha's statue toppling]]. [https://www.tiranatimes.com/opposition-protests-mark-renewed-political-tensions-in-albania/ (Tirana Times)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/graft-allegations-spark-clashes-albania-between-police-protesters-2026-02-20/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Winter Olympics]]
**[[Norway at the Olympics|Norway]] breaks the record for [[All-time Olympic Games medal table|most gold medals]] at a single [[Winter Olympics]] event after skier [[Johannes Dale-Skjevdal]] won the country's 17th gold medal in [[Milan]]–[[Cortina d'Ampezzo|Cortina]], surpassing their own record of 16 gold medals. [https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/winter-olympics/norway-gold-medals-olympics-dale-skjevdal-biathlon-b2924477.html (''The Independent'')]
